title: ESP tests in a Faraday cage at the Round Table

tellings.quote: built a Faraday cage there and I think you know, was one of the first people as far as I understand doing ESP tests in a in a Faraday cage

plain: In the early 1950s, at the Round Table Foundation, a research group in Rockland, Maine, someone is said to have built a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks electrical and radio signals, and used it for some of the first tests of extrasensory perception inside one. A researcher named Greg Malatzi tells Michels this as he understands it, without naming a source. The point of such a test would be to show that a mind could pick up information that no radio signal could carry.
